extracted.intended_audience: USPTO financial statement preparers, federal accountants, auditors, OMB/oversight staff, and agency management
extracted.subtask_description: Accounting policy and disclosure guidance used to prepare the USPTO consolidated financial statements and notes, including presentation, recognition, valuation, and classification rules consistent with GAAP and OMB Circular A-136. Intended to support consistent preparation, auditability, and oversight of USPTO financial reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The accompanying financial statements present the financial position, net cost of operations, and budgetary resources for the USPTO prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP) and the form and content for entity financial statements specified by OMB Circular A-136, as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books and records of the USPTO serve as the source of information. Statements may differ from other reports submitted pursuant to OMB directives for monitoring/controlling budgetary use. GAAP for federal entities are the standards prescribed by the Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation by Program
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO presents cost of operations by program consistent with the agency’s strategic plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program costs consist of both costs related directly to individual strategic goals and overall support costs allocated to the strategic goals. All costs are assigned to specific programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of Intra-governmental vs. Public
rubrics_metrics.description: Assets, liabilities, revenues, and costs are classified according to the type of entity with which the transactions are associated (intra-governmental vs. with the public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intra-governmental assets/liabilities are those from or to other federal entities; intra-governmental earned revenues are collections or accruals from other federal entities and intra-governmental costs are payments or accruals to other federal entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance Sheet Format Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance Sheet format has been changed to reflect more detail for certain line items as required for significant reporting entities by OMB Circular A-136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change allows readers to see how amounts on the Balance Sheet are reflected on the Government-wide Balance Sheet and supports preparation and audit of the Financial Report of the United States Government. Prior year balances may be reclassified to conform with current presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Function Classification and Authority Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal budget classifies the USPTO under the Other Advancement of Commerce (376) budget function; the USPTO does not have lending or borrowing authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO does not transact business among its own operating units (except immaterial transactions) and therefore no intra-entity eliminations are necessary. The USPTO does not receive allocation transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax Status
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is not subject to federal, state, or local income taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly, no provision for income taxes is recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified Activities Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounting standards allow presentations/disclosures to be modified to prevent disclosure of classified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities must disclose that such modifications are permitted when needed to protect classified information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of Accounting (Accrual and Budgetary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements reflect both accrual and budgetary accounting transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under accrual accounting, revenues recognized when earned and expenses when incurred. Budgetary accounting recognizes obligations according to legal requirements, often prior to accrual-based transactions; essential for compliance with legal constraints and controls over federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funds from Dedicated Collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds from dedicated collections are financed by specifically identified revenues required by statute to be used for designated activities and must be accounted for separately from the government’s general revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the USPTO, funds from dedicated collections include the salaries and expenses fund, fee reserve fund, and the special fund receipts. Additional details provided in Note 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiduciary Activities Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiduciary activities are not recognized on the financial statements; they are reported on schedules in the notes to the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiduciary balances are not assets of the federal government. At the USPTO, fiduciary activities are recorded in the Patent Cooperation Treaty fund and the Madrid Protocol fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect reported amounts and disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual results could differ from estimates. Estimates affect assets, liabilities, contingent assets/liabilities, and revenues/expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange Revenue Recognition and Fee Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees remitted with initial applications and requests for services are recorded as exchange revenue when received, with adjustment to defer revenue for services not yet performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual maintenance and renewal fees are recorded when received and help recoup prior costs. Amounts remitted without a request for service are recorded as liabilities in customer deposit accounts until services are ordered. Director fee-setting authority under AIA section 10 allows fee adjustments to recover aggregate USPTO costs; individual fees may be set at, below, or above cost if aggregate cost recovery is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and Gifts-in-Kind Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial gifts and gifts-in-kind received by USPTO are included in the consolidated Gifts and Bequests Fund financial statements of the Department of Commerce and are not reflected in the USPTO’s financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most gifts-in-kind are used for official travel to further the USPTO mission and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputed Financing Sources for Costs Absorbed by Others
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating costs paid in full or in part by other federal entities are recognized as imputed costs and an Imputed Financing Source from Cost Absorbed by Others is recognized on the Statements of Changes in Net Position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include CSRS pension benefits paid by OPM, legal judgments paid from the Judgment Fund, and electronic fee collection costs paid by Treasury. Applicable imputed costs are included on Statements of Net Cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers In/Out Accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Intragovernmental transfers of budget authority without reimbursement are recorded at book value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity vs Non-Entity Asset Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Entity assets are those an entity is authorized to use in operations; non-entity assets are held by an entity but are not available for the entity’s use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most USPTO assets are entity assets except portions of Fund Balance with Treasury and cash/monetary assets. Non-entity assets (e.g., customer deposit accounts) are disclosed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund Balance with Treasury Operations
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO deposits fees in commercial bank accounts maintained by the Treasury’s Bureau of the Fiscal Service; monies are transferred to the Federal Reserve the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many customer deposits are wired directly to the Federal Reserve. Banking activity is conducted per BFS directives; Treasury processes all disbursements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounts Receivable Establishment and Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts receivable balances are established for amounts owed by employees and governmental entities; the USPTO requires payment prior to provision of most services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowance for uncollectible receivables is established for receivables older than two years with little/no collection activity that have been transferred to Treasury. Intergovernmental receivables are regarded as fully collectable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances and Prepayments Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO prepays amounts in anticipation of future benefits; an expense is not recorded until goods are received or services performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepayments occur with both governmental and non-governmental vendors. Examples include deposit accounts for recurring transactions, postage, centralized services, maintenance agreements, and subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash and Other Monetary Assets Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash and other monetary assets include checks, electronic funds transfer, and credit card payments in transit and undeposited checks that are not credited at the Balance Sheet date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undeposited check amounts are considered cash equivalents. Customer deposit accounts with the public are disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property, Plant, and Equipment Capitalization and Depreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization thresholds and asset classes are established (IT equipment, software, software in development, furniture, equipment, leasehold improvements) with specified thresholds (e.g., $50k individual, $250k bulk). Costs capitalized at historical cost and depreciated on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leasehold improvements depreciated over remaining life of lease or useful life, whichever is shorter. Software development costs (design, coding, testing) capitalized and not amortized until placed in service. Acquisitions not meeting criteria are expensed on receipt. Useful lives updated prospectively as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workers' Compensation Accounting (FECA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for FECA benefits for USPTO employees are administered by DOL and ultimately paid by the USPTO; DOL bills USPTO annually but payment is deferred approximately two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actuarial liability is estimated by DOL using procedures to include death, disability, medical, miscellaneous costs, and incurred-but-not-reported claims; liability updated annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unemployment Compensation Billing
rubrics_metrics.description: Unemployment compensation benefits for USPTO employees are administered by DOL; DOL bills each agency quarterly as claims are paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave Accrual Accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual leave and compensatory time are accrued as earned and reduced when leave is taken; sick and other non-vested leave is expensed as used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly adjustments ensure accrued leave accounts reflect current pay rates. If current year funding unavailable to pay for leave earned but not taken, funding will be obtained from future financing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee Retirement and Post-Employment Benefits Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees participate in CSRS or FERS; USPTO financial statements do not report CSRS/FERS assets, accumulated plan benefits, or liabilities — OPM administers and reports those amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO recognizes a funded expense for its share of costs to the federal government of providing pension and post-retirement benefits and recognizes an imputed cost for OPM’s share. USPTO makes current year contributions (percentages provided) and makes Thrift Savings Plan mandatory and matching contributions per FERS rules; no matching for CSRS employees. Any difference between OPM funding and reporting factors is recognized as an imputed cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred Revenue Measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferred revenue represents fees received for services not substantially completed; two types are recorded: checks received not yet deposited and fees for partially processed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferred revenue balance is estimated by analyzing process completion for each service; percent incomplete based on inventory of pending work and completion status is applied to fee collections to estimate deferred revenue. Deferred revenue is affected by changes in patent/trademark filings, first action pendency rates, and fee rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net Position Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Net Position is the residual difference between assets and liabilities and is composed of Cumulative Results of Operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cumulative Results of Operations is the net result of the USPTO’s operations since inception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Cleanup Liabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO discloses environmental cleanup liabilities; in this reporting period the USPTO does not have any known liabilities for environmental cleanup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liabilities Covered vs Not Covered by Budgetary Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO records liabilities for likely payments as a result of events that have occurred; liabilities covered by budgetary resources are funded by realized budgetary resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realized budgetary resources include obligated balances and unobligated balances (operating reserve) as of year-end. Liabilities not covered by budgetary resources may be probable but require Congressional action before budgetary resources can be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of Deferred Revenue (Patent/Trademark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferred revenue disclosures break out unearned fees and undeposited checks by patent and trademark totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables present balances by category and year to support transparency of deferred revenue components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Employee Benefits Payable Valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: FECA actuarial liability is calculated annually by DOL and projected annual payments are discounted to present value using an average of the Treasury’s Yield Curve for Nominal Coupon issues over current and prior four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest rate assumptions for wage and medical benefits are disclosed for the year in question. USPTO’s liability estimates provided based on DOL information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating Lease Accounting and Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: GSA negotiates long-term office leases and levies rent charges approximate to commercial rental rates; operating lease agreements are cancelable and expire at various dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leases and future minimum lease payments are disclosed by fiscal year and lease location; commitments primarily relate to headquarters and regional offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments and Contingencies Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO is party to routine administrative proceedings and legal actions; management discloses reasonably possible or probable amounts for claims and litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose amounts that are reasonably possible or probable and provide context (e.g., expected payments for labor relations claims, suits where adverse outcome probable). Note whether any payments were made from the Judgment Fund and whether there are major long-term commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Employment Benefits Expense Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-employment benefit expenses (CSRS, FERS, FEHB, FEGLI, FICA) are presented with funded and imputed amounts and totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose amounts for funded, imputed, and total costs for each benefit category and trends year-over-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funds from Dedicated Collections Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds from dedicated collections are financed by specifically identified revenues and must be accounted for separately; at USPTO these include the salaries and expenses fund, the fee reserve fund, and special fund receipts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-entity funds are excluded from amounts disclosed for funds from dedicated collections; further details provided in Note 14.
